notes: Main disagreements: (1) actor, mostly all or admin versus instructor for advice and rationale sentences; resolved by who the sentence is addressed to (instructor when it is advice to faculty choosing or teaching, all for facts about tools or students, admin for the committee's own commitments). (2) phase, general versus before-course/course-start/during-work; resolved by when the act happens (asking before using AI and fallback rules during-work, syllabus statements course-start, provenance, scope and limits-of-control statements general). (3) modality: the source verb decides (must for 'we must teach', should-not for 'should assume ... is prohibited', may for 'might look like'); classification sentences ('shall be treated similarly to ... plagiarism') are informs. (4) policy_type: P83 vs P35 for reassessing outcomes and assignments (P35), P79 vs P35 for directing students to use AI on an assignment (P79), P12 vs P14 for literature summaries (P14), P63 vs P09 for hosted sample syllabus statements (P63), P88 vs UNCOVERED for the communication plan and central page (UNCOVERED), P62 vs UNCOVERED for the reproducibility concern (UNCOVERED). (5) unit_stance (not scored): disclosure conditions coded permit rather than require or encourage; detector privacy risk neutral. (6) Anchors: several were cut mid-clause, so fuller anchors or normalized policies were used; the prompt/tool/date research reporting bullets were merged into one unit (one unit, counted as one matched pair). Only-A units kept (13): three scope/provenance or teaching-priority sentences, the ban sample position, the assignment-level choice sentence, the adoption survey (recoded UNCOVERED), peer benchmarking, enterprise-security warning, LLM unreliability sentence, chemical-compound disclosure, enterprise-AI exploration, and three Delphi sentences (assessments disconnected from context, 'showing up is more interesting', multilingual false positives). Only-B units kept (18) and dropped (1): kept the sample position 2 heading, instructor-variation sentence, AI-tutor practice, translation, teaching obligation, teaching paramount, wary of false positives, legal-violation warning, hallucination sentence, passing off AI output, literature-search limit, enterprise-AI investigation, tool portal (recoded UNCOVERED), computing infrastructure, Delphi resourcing, ITS resourcing, and two Delphi sentences (safeguards in asynchronous courses, voice-memo assignments). Dropped: the Academic Dishonesty preamble rationale, which is not AI-specific. Document stance agreed on both documents (delegates). Counts: 100 matched pairs across the two documents.
